Commands: only the app owner turns the connector and its approved writes on or off, with `benmore mcp status|enable|disable <app> [--writes] [--auto-approve] [--export] [--publication] [--revoke] [--env dev|prod]` or the platform tool `mcp_connector` {app, action, writes, auto_approve, export, publication, revoke, authorized, env}. status takes no switch flag, --revoke applies to a plain disable only, and enable --auto-approve requires --writes. Any collaborator may read `status` (switch booleans only); enable and disable stay owner-only. `benmore mcp status|enable|disable` takes an explicit <app> from any directory and otherwise uses the workspace's .benmore/app. When the app has a dev instance, env is required for enable and disable.

Tool authorization: the tool's enable, in any form, requires authorized:true, passed only when the human explicitly asked for it in this session (refused before any side effect otherwise); status and disable (including --revoke) need no authorization because they only remove access, and the CLI is the human path.

enable: enable exposes the connector (a reviewed mcp.yaml must be loaded). enable --writes also installs and verifies revision enrollment and turns approved writes on; it refuses, leaving writes off and exposure as it was, when the reviewed manifest fails its check, declares no command tools, or enrollment cannot be installed or verified (a pending enrollment left by an interrupted attempt needs an operator repair; a stale, retired or changed one is re-enrolled by this enable --writes).

disable: disable --writes turns writes off and keeps exposure (and the revision ledger, which exposed reads cite); disable turns both off and removes the revision triggers and ledger, tombstones included, so the app's own writes stop feeding them (start-up also removes a ledger left by a disabled connector or by an mcp.yaml since removed, turning approved writes off); the next enable --writes re-enrolls through repair, a fresh incarnation seeded from the current rows, so row revisions restart. Disable pauses; grants survive re-enable.

revoke: use --revoke to invalidate every connected client: disable --revoke also rotates the read epoch, so every connector grant and token stops working for good, and deletes every user's stored external connection credential (irreversible: every client must reconnect and be approved again, and users re-enter connection credentials), and a later enable --writes re-enrolls the retired revision enrollment.

Turning writes off: it takes effect for the next call and permanently voids every operation prepared or approved but not yet committed (the write epoch rotates, so even a later re-enable never runs it); stored operations, receipts and audit rows are kept, and a plain disable keeps the read epoch and grants.

Restarts: a process restart (including a runtime upgrade) first turns approved writes off and rotates the write epoch, because a new process may carry new code, migrations or environment; it then resumes them, with no owner action, only when the owner state still records the contract and execution digests the owner approved writes under, the loaded reviewed manifest carries those same digests, read exposure is on, and the revision enrollment is active for the current owner epoch and verifies against the database. Operations prepared or approved before the restart never run after it. Anything else leaves writes off, and mcp status then reports approved_writes_off_reason (a fixed phrase: stale mcp.yaml review, changed reviewed digests, unverified enrollment); run enable --writes to approve again. disable --writes, disable, --revoke, a restore, a hot reload and an environment change forget the approval, so a later restart never resumes them. Enrollment is never created or repaired at start-up.

status: status reports exposed, approved_writes, manifest validity, command tool count and revision enrollment (none, pending, active, stale, retired, changed, out_of_order, or unavailable with a problem line when the state cannot be read). `changed` is explained in `diagnostics` (1) and `out_of_order` in `revision_trigger_order`. On a host where the operator has not set up connector storage for the instance, status reports it unconfigured and enable refuses.

Audit: each enable or disable, including a refused one, writes an app audit row (action mcp_connector_switch: the owner's platform identity and before/after booleans, never an epoch) plus a platform activity entry.

Export and publication: owner-only external_export and public_publication switches default off, are controlled with benmore mcp enable|disable --export/--publication or mcp_connector flags, are audited, and rotate a per-capability generation on disable so queued effects cannot revive after re-enable.
Table rebuild: a forced table rebuild by the migrator replays the connector revision triggers; the revision enrollment then fails verification until explicit repair.
